questions.stem: In which state of matter are particles arranged in a regular pattern with fixed positions?
questions.explanation: In a solid, particles are arranged in a regular pattern and held in fixed positions by strong forces. They can only vibrate about their fixed positions.

questions.stem: Which state of matter has no fixed shape and no fixed volume?
questions.explanation: Gases have no fixed shape or volume. The particles move rapidly in all directions and spread out to fill any container they are placed in.

questions.stem: Why can liquids flow but solids cannot?

options.text: Because liquids are always lighter than solids
Because liquid particles have no forces between them
Because liquid particles can move past each other, while solid particles are held in fixed positions
Because liquid particles are smaller than solid particles

questions.explanation: In liquids, the particles are close together but can move past each other, allowing the liquid to flow. In solids, particles are held in fixed positions by strong forces and can only vibrate.

questions.stem: Why are gases easily compressed but solids and liquids are not?

options.text: Because gas particles have large spaces between them that can be reduced

questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart with large spaces between them. These spaces can be reduced when pressure is applied, making gases compressible. In solids and liquids, particles are already close together.

questions.stem: What happens to the movement of particles as temperature increases?

options.text: Particles move faster and have more kinetic energy

questions.explanation: As temperature increases, particles gain more kinetic energy and move faster. This is true for all three states of matter.

questions.stem: Which state of matter has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container?
questions.explanation: Liquids have a fixed volume because their particles are close together, but they take the shape of their container because the particles can move past each other.

questions.stem: In the particle model, what do the forces between particles represent?

options.text: The attractive forces (bonds or intermolecular forces) that hold particles together

questions.explanation: The forces between particles include both chemical bonds within substances and intermolecular forces between molecules. These forces determine the state of the substance at a given temperature.
